message.content: I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy within the mandate. The report showed a fundamentally sound, cash-generative business: total net sales of $391.0 billion (up 2% year over year), operating income of $123.2 billion (up from $114.3 billion), operating cash flow of $118.3 billion, and diluted EPS of $6.08. Net income of $93.7 billion was down versus the prior year, but the decline was driven almost entirely by a one-time, non-cash-operational $10.2 billion net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid Decision—underlying profitability actually improved, with gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1% and Services revenue growing 13% to $96.2 billion, while the company held $140.8 billion in cash and marketable securities and returned roughly $110 billion to shareholders via buybacks and dividends. With the stock trading around $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) and fundamentals strong, I placed one buy order for 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00 (about $9,812, comfortably under the $10,000 per-order cap). This keeps me within all mandate constraints: AAPL is an eligible name, it's a buy order, limit is ~0.1% above the current market, today's total outlay of ~$9,812 is well under the $20,000 daily cap, and no money was moved out of the account (cash covered the purchase). The order filled at $223.00.
